metadata.source: SAMHSA, NIMH, American Psychological Association, CDC
metadata.description: Evidence-based mental health treatments for youth
metadata.note: Effectiveness percentages based on clinical trials and meta-analyses

treatments.name: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT)
treatments.description: Evidence-based talk therapy focusing on changing negative thought patterns and behaviors. Highly effective for youth.
treatments.considerations: Requires motivated participant; may take 8-12 weeks to see full benefits

treatments.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
treatments.description: Specialized therapy combining CBT with mindfulness and acceptance strategies. Excellent for self-harm and emotional regulation.
treatments.considerations: More intensive; requires 1-2 years commitment; best for moderate-severe cases

treatments.name: Family-Based Treatment (FBT)
treatments.description: Involves parents/guardians in treatment to improve family dynamics and support systems. Highly effective for younger youth.
treatments.considerations: Requires family involvement; may reveal family conflicts

treatments.name: Interpersonal Therapy (IPT)
treatments.description: Focuses on improving interpersonal relationships and addressing social isolation. Particularly effective for depression.
treatments.considerations: Best for depression with social component; requires some social engagement capacity

treatments.name: Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors (SSRIs)
treatments.description: First-line antidepressants. FDA-approved for youth depression and anxiety. Should be combined with therapy.
treatments.considerations: Requires medical supervision; black box warning on suicidal thoughts in early treatment; works best with therapy

treatments.name: Combination Therapy + Medication
treatments.description: Gold standard treatment: psychotherapy combined with medication. Superior outcomes vs. either alone.
treatments.considerations: Requires coordinated care between therapist and psychiatrist; most resource-intensive

treatments.name: Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy (MBCT)
treatments.description: Combines mindfulness practices with cognitive therapy. Effective for preventing relapse and managing stress.
treatments.considerations: Requires consistent attendance; group setting not suitable for all; benefits build over time

treatments.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
treatments.description: Evidence-based therapy teaching acceptance of thoughts/feelings while pursuing valued activities.
treatments.considerations: Different approach than CBT; requires willingness to experience discomfort; growing evidence base

treatments.name: School-Based Mental Health Programs
treatments.description: Universal prevention programs delivered in schools. Includes counseling, screening, and early intervention.
treatments.considerations: Variable quality; resource-dependent; best as complement to individual treatment

treatments.name: Peer Support Groups
treatments.description: Groups of youth with similar experiences. Provides validation, reduces isolation, builds coping skills.
treatments.considerations: Varies by group quality; works best as complement to professional treatment; not substitute for therapy

treatments.name: Exercise and Physical Activity
treatments.description: Regular physical activity (30+ min, 5x/week). Evidence shows benefits comparable to antidepressants for mild-moderate depression.
treatments.considerations: Requires consistency; may be difficult for severe depression; best combined with other treatments

treatments.name: Sleep Hygiene and Sleep Therapy
treatments.description: Addressing sleep problems through behavioral interventions and consistent sleep schedules. Critical for mental health.
treatments.considerations: Requires habit change; initial adjustment period; may need behavioral therapist guidance

treatments.name: Nutrition and Diet Intervention
treatments.description: Dietary changes supporting mental health: Mediterranean diet, omega-3 supplementation. Evidence growing.
treatments.considerations: Emerging evidence; should not replace evidence-based therapies; cultural dietary considerations

treatments.name: Social Skills Training
treatments.description: Teaches youth to build relationships, communicate effectively, and manage social situations.
treatments.considerations: Often part of larger treatment package; practice needed between sessions; group format enhances learning

treatments.name: Crisis Intervention and Safety Planning
treatments.description: Crisis lines, safety plans, and emergency interventions for acute mental health crises. Essential for severe cases.
treatments.considerations: For emergencies only; not substitute for ongoing treatment; follow-up care essential
